title: Router/PreActivation: Multiple Resolvers resolving to empty observables cause uncaught EmptyError

## Current behavior When there is a route with more than one resolver, empty observables (no next, only complete, as in EmptyObservable) are treated differently than with a single resolver: - if for example 1 of 2 resolvers resolves to an empty observable, the navigation is not canceled, but the corresponding route-data-field is undefined as result - if all resolvers resolve to empty observables, navigation is canceled, but due to an uncaught EmptyError, because the combined resolvers are piped through a last() operator ## Expected behavior - if any resolver resolves to empty, navigation must be canceled, as it is the behaviour for a single resolver - even if all resolvers resolve to empty, the router should not emit any uncaught errors ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions 1. open: https://angular-gitter-enmoca.stackblitz.io 2. click the link and observe an uncaught EmptyError in the browser console the interesting code is in app.module.ts, it configures a route with two resolves that resolve to EMPTY ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? In our case, we have implemented an error consuming procedure that takes care of any failures during resolver actions (like http errors), thus in case of an error it is important to be able to indicate route cancellation without forwarding an error to the router. (a) Because if a resolver cannot obtain what it is supposed to obtain, we do not want to navigate, because the destination page would be empty/broken. (b) we treat uncaught errors as potential bugs (and have set up an error handler accordingly). An error from a resolver ends up as uncaught error, which would be wrong in the case of a handled http failure. (c) This resolving to "nothing" with am empty observable is just the right way to indicate navigation shall be cancelled but no error should end up in the console. As it is already the case with single resolvers. ## Environment 

Angular version: 5.2.9
Also in Angular 6, see the angular-gitter link.

Others:
I belive the problem is the implementation of resolveNode in PreActivation. It should rather combine multiple resolvers using the semantics of Observable.combineLatest(...) and the takeLast(1) operator, because last() causes the EmptyError... but i have no further knowledge of the angular codebase, so that is just my 2 cents.
